title: Cross-stitch rose on linen
subtitle: A blowsy garden rose in five pinks on 28-count antique white linen
excerpt: A fully-open garden rose in five shades of pink and cream on 28-count antique white linen. The design is approximately 70 by 70 stitches and finishes at roughly 12 by 12 cm when worked over two threads. The petals are shaded from deep rose at the centre out to the palest blush at the outer edge.
sourceNotes: Original design. Shaded rose designs have been a staple of British cross-stitch publishing since the Victorian era. Therese de Dillmont's Encyclopedia of Needlework (Project Gutenberg #20776) includes shaded floral embroidery as a primary technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fabric woven with individual threads of equal weight in both directions, unlike Aida's grouped thread blocks. Cross-stitch on evenweave is worked over two threads in each direction, so a 28-count evenweave gives the same stitch size as 14-count Aida.

content.text: Linen gives this rose a soft, painterly quality that Aida does not. The
background is worked over two threads in each direction; the shading is achieved by working the five pinks in concentric zones from the tight spiral centre outward.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 3685 (very dark mauve), 3687 (mauve), 3688 (medium mauve), 3689 (light mauve), 819 (light baby pink), 3865 (white), 469 (avocado green), 470 (light avocado green), 471 (very light avocado green), 3787 (dark warm grey)

content.text: Begin at the tight inner centre.
Stitch the innermost curled petals in 3685 (darkest). The centre is a small spiral of roughly five to eight stitches across on the chart.
Work outward through the petal zones.
Move through 3687, 3688, 3689, and finally 819 as you progress outward to the outer petals. Each petal takes approximately two to three colour changes from its base to its outer edge.
Add the outer petal edges in blended thread.
For the very outer edges of the outermost petals, thread one strand of 819 with one strand of 3865 in the needle. The blend creates a near-white edge without a hard colour break.
Fill leaves in 469 and 470, with 471 for the lightest highlight zones. Stem in 469 back-stitch.
Work the petal outline in back-stitch last.
Use one strand of 3787 to outline each petal. The grey outline is softer than black against the pink tones and suits the linen background.
Wash gently in cool water. Press face-down, pulling the linen square. Frame in a 15 × 15 cm square mount or a 12 cm round mount for a circular framed finish.
